chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhraz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not pray over the drowned one of the wine.'
ai.seo_question: Who does the Prophet not pray over according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) specifies that he does not perform the funeral prayer over one who drowned while intoxicated, highlighting the interplay between the manner of death and the state of the deceased. Shia jurists, such as Al-Tusi, utilize this narration to discuss whether the 'drowning' (*gharaq*) refers to the physical cause or the spiritual state of being overwhelmed by sin, often linking it to the broader concept of *mawt al-jahiliyyah* (death in ignorance). This ruling underscores the significance of ritual purity and conscious faith in the final moments of life for receiving full communal prayers.
